hero.headline: Apex Motorsport Series
hero.subhead: A structured racing league with a real ladder — F1, F2, F3 and GT3 — run with contracts, stewards and a live roster that updates itself.

about.title: Who are we?
paragraphs: AMS — the Apex Motorsport Series — is a Roblox racing league built like a real motorsport series rather than a pickup lobby. Drivers race in FR26 (Formula 2026 Racing) and GTM across four divisions, and every seat is a real role: sign with a team, hold a number, and your name appears on the live lineups below.

The league runs a ladder. F3 and F2 exist so new drivers have somewhere to learn without being thrown straight into a championship fight, and race control means results are decided by stewards reading incidents — not by who shouted loudest.
What started in July 2026 is now 226 members, 41 team entries across four divisions, and a calendar with mandatory pit stops and defined pit windows.

features.title: What we have
features.intro: Everything that makes a season feel like a season, not a series of lobbies.

items.title: A four-tier grid
items.text: F1, F2, F3 and GT3 — 41 team entries between them, with an F4 division prepared for next season.

items.title: Real contracts
items.text: Every signing is logged with division, team, role and contract length (maximum two seasons). Free agents are visible to every team owner.

items.title: Race weekend structure
items.text: Each round has a briefing: lap count, one mandatory stop, and a numbered pit window.

items.title: Race control and stewarding
items.text: A president, directors, assistants and stewards, plus a safety car driver. Incidents are protested and judged, not argued out in chat.

items.title: Live lineups
items.text: This page reads the same file the bot publishes whenever a role changes, so the roster on screen is the roster on the grid.

items.title: Lap-time boards
items.text: A forum of verified times per circuit — the league's own benchmark rather than a guess.

items.title: Team garages
items.text: Each team gets a private HQ, livery space and a contract area inside the server.

items.title: Staff and media paths
items.text: Moderation applications are reviewed weekly, alongside media, graphics and commentary roles.

divisions.title: The grid
divisions.intro: Four divisions, one ladder. Grid slots are counted from the server's own team roles.
divisions.note: F3 is the easiest place to start: nine teams and plenty of open seats.

calendar.title: Season 1 calendar
calendar.intro: Every round runs to one mandatory stop inside a published pit window.

rules.title: The rules, in short
rules.intro: The full rules live in the server. These are the five that get you removed.
items: No racism — including slurs in text, stickers or GIFs, and anything targeting skin colour or nationality.
Respect the staff — they run the league.
Use channels for their purpose — fun-race talk belongs in the fun-race channel.
No doxxing — no addresses, names, faces or private information.

join.title: How to join

steps.title: Join the Discord
steps.text: Everything happens there: signings, race briefings, stewarding and the lap-time boards.

steps.title: Verify
steps.text: Verification links your Roblox username to your Discord name so teams know who they are signing.

steps.title: Get on the grid
steps.text: Pick a division, talk to team owners, or list yourself as a free agent. Contracts are signed publicly with team, role, length and nationality.

steps.title: Prefer the paddock?
steps.text: Moderation, media, graphics and stewarding roles are open, with applications reviewed every Thursday.

join.inviteNote: Ask any staff member for the current invite link.

items.q: Do I need a powerful PC?
items.a: No. Everything runs on Roblox, in FR26 (Formula 2026 Racing) and GTM.

items.q: I've never raced in a league before. Can I still join?
items.a: Yes. F3 is deliberately the entry tier and F4 is being prepared, so most of the grid has room for new drivers.
Yes — there are free team owner and team principal roles, and existing teams recruit throughout the season.
There is an incidents forum. Stewards review each report, and only race officials can issue penalties — anything a session host decides is provisional.
A maximum of two seasons, logged publicly in the signings channel.
The server has Europe and Asia roles and runs in English.

footer.text: Built and run by the AMS staff team. Lineups update automatically from Discord roles.
